4115268.title: QUAD, Questions of Theatre: Why the Rooftop Peppers Went Missing
4115268.overview: A play staged at Daehangno Theatre QUAD, the Seoul Foundation for Arts and Culture's venue in the university theatre district. In a shabby multi-family house on the edge of Seoul, an old woman named Gwangja grows chilli peppers in a small rooftop plot, until one summer day every pepper vanishes. The thief turns out to be a neighbour, Hyeonja, and what looks like a trivial theft becomes, to the man in unit 301, a symptom of a world falling apart. Only one other resident is willing to act with him, and a squabble over peppers grows into an uproar that takes in the whole building. Performed in Korean. Weekdays 19:30, weekends and holidays 15:00; no performances on Mondays.
4115268.fee: 50,000 won, all seats (discounts on the official site)
4115268.hours: Weekdays 19:30 · Weekends and holidays 15:00 · No Monday performances
4115268.sponsor: Seoul Foundation for Arts and Culture, Daehangno Theatre QUAD

2855326.title: Ureuk Cultural Festival
2855326.overview: Chungju's main arts festival, held since 1971 in the name of Ureuk, the sixth-century master musician credited with the gayageum, and staged where he is said to have played: Tangeum Park on the Namhan River. The 54th edition runs from 8 to 11 October under the slogan 'Chungju's tomorrow in the resonance of Ureuk', with a 'newtro' theme that reworks 1980s and 90s culture. Traditional and contemporary performances share the stages with arts competitions, exhibitions and hands-on programmes, and young local artists show and sell their work. A market of Chungju farm produce and food runs throughout. Free, at Tangeum Park and the Chungju Culture Center.
2855326.place: Tangeum Park and Chungju Culture Center
2855326.sponsor: Korean Federation of Arts and Culture Organizations, Chungju Branch

2854507.title: Wando Autumn Island Festival
2854507.overview: Wando, the island county at the far south-west tip of the mainland, runs an autumn festival built around its famous abalone and its outlying islands. At the beach park in the county town there is an abalone tasting and sales hall with flash auctions and discounts, local food and culture stalls, and stage programmes from an opening show and a 'romantic autumn island' concert to a singing contest, a bubble magic show and local bands. Island programmes tie in Cheongsando, Bogildo and Saengildo, the Wando Arboretum holds a forest festival, and there are guided walks on stages 86 to 88 of the Namparang coastal trail. Free.

1719667.title: Nakdonggang Gupo Naru Festival
1719667.overview: Gupo was the great river port of the lower Nakdong, and Busan's Buk-gu district celebrates it each October at Hwamyeong Ecological Park, a stretch of lotus ponds and riverbank on the city's north-west edge. The 13th edition runs from 16 to 18 October under the slogan 'connect, play, meet at Gupo Naru'. A reconstructed ferry landing recalls the old port; Gupo's famous noodles are served as platters and made in noodle-pulling workshops; there are ecology and wellness programmes, a riverside book fair, a singing contest and open busking by residents. After dark the park lights up with a night walk, a garden of lights and a night market. Free, with some paid activities.
1719667.addr: 1455 Nakdonggang Bicycle Path, Deokcheon-dong, Buk-gu, Busan
1719667.place: Lotus complex, Hwamyeong Ecological Park, Buk-gu, Busan

4115205.title: Seoul Petlympic 2026
4115205.overview: A dog-sports festival for citizens and their dogs on the Peace Plaza of World Cup Park in Sangam, 24 and 25 October. The 'Petlympic' events are designed for beginners as much as competitors: stay, recall, a cone slalom and a 15-metre sprint, plus a 4 km Dog Trail walk. Around them, agility, frisbee, dog dancing and flyball teams compete and demonstrate, and there are drop-in programmes, activity booths and rest areas for the whole day. Entry is free; the two Petlympic events and the Dog Trail each cost 40,000 won to enter.
4115205.fee: Free entry · Petlympic events (two) 40,000 won · Dog Trail 40,000 won

4115269.title: QUAD, Questions of Theatre: Dance of Revolution
4115269.overview: A play at Daehangno Theatre QUAD that abandons conventional narrative for eight independent scenes, each a fragment from the middle of a revolution, none linked by cause and effect. What holds them together is repetition: lines and sounds, objects and light, and the actors' precisely patterned movement recur until a hidden structure surfaces, and the audience senses connections between the scenes on a level beyond story. Performed in Korean. Weekdays 19:30, weekends and holidays 15:00; no performances on Mondays or Tuesdays.

4115275.title: QUAD, Questions of Theatre: Incendies
4115275.overview: A Korean-language production of Wajdi Mouawad's Incendies (Scorched) at Daehangno Theatre QUAD. Twins Jeanne and Simon, whose mother Nawal spent her last five years in silence, open her will to find two impossible instructions: deliver letters to a father they believed dead and a brother they never knew existed, and bury her without coffin or headstone. Following her traces, they move step by step into her past and, at the end of it, the devastating truth behind her silence. Performed in Korean. Weekdays 19:30, weekends 15:00, with an 18:00 performance on Saturday 14 November; no performances on Mondays.

4115201.title: Daejeon Citizens' Energy Walk (WCPEC-9)
4115201.overview: A free, non-competitive walk on 15 November marking Daejeon's hosting of the World Conference on Photovoltaic Energy Conversion. Walkers set off from Expo Citizens' Plaza and loop through the Hanbat Arboretum, completing four QR-code stamp missions on their phones for a finisher's reward and a digital certificate. Energy-themed programmes and activities run alongside. A pleasant autumn afternoon in the city's central parkland, open to anyone.
4115201.sponsor: Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment, Daejeon Metropolitan City, Korean Photovoltaic Society

4115260.title: QUAD, Questions of Theatre: Train to Xi'an
4115260.overview: A play at Daehangno Theatre QUAD. On a train racing toward the tomb of the First Emperor outside Xi'an, a Korean man with a Chinese mother thinks about the terracotta army he is about to see and about a ruler who wanted to live forever. Set against that vast appetite for immortality are his own small, unanswered wants, above all a love that was never fully returned; a life lived at the margins looks at itself in front of the largest story it knows. Performed in Korean. Weekdays 19:30, weekends 15:00; no performances on Mondays.
4115260.fee: 50,000 won, all seats (discounts on the official site)
4115260.sponsor: Seoul Foundation for Arts and Culture, Daehangno Theatre QUAD
